title: A cup of cold water (Matthew 10:34–42)
hook: a speech that opens with a sword ends with a glass of water
tomorrow: what if people complain no matter what you do?

segments.voice: Yesterday: sheep among wolves, and two animals to carry at once, the serpent's clear eyes and the dove's gentle hands. Wise and harmless. Now, how that same speech ends.

A hot afternoon at practice, and somebody tosses a cold water bottle down the bleachers to the kid on the end. Nobody will remember it by Friday. Except the kid who was thirsty. Now a different doorway. Twelve men are about to leave with no purse and no spare coat, and Jesus is finishing their instructions. It has been hard listening: wolves, councils, being hated. Then the hardest line of all: "Think not that I am come to send peace on earth: I came not to send peace, but a sword." They're still standing at the door. How does a speech like that end?
screen: `A WATER BOTTLE DOWN THE BLEACHERS.` → `TWELVE AT THE DOOR.` → `NOT PEACE, BUT A SWORD.`

segments.voice: Not on the sword. The next lines show what the sword cuts: a household divided over him, a man set at variance against his father. Then the cost gets personal: "He that findeth his life shall lose it: and he that loseth his life for my sake shall find it." And then the speech turns around. Jesus stops talking about the road and starts talking about the doors that will open to them: "He that receiveth you receiveth me, and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me." A welcome travels up a chain, from a stranger's doorstep all the way to God. The last link is the smallest: "whosoever shall give to drink unto one of these little ones a cup of cold water only in the name of a disciple, verily I say unto you, he shall in no wise lose his reward." Notice the word only. Not a feast. Not a guest room. A cup. Some readers hear the little ones as the disciples themselves, sent out small and empty-handed; others hear anyone small and in need. Either way, here's one to tell a friend tonight: the speech that opens with a sword closes with a glass of water, and the glass is the part Jesus promises will be remembered.
screen: `THE SWORD: A HOUSEHOLD DIVIDED.` · `LOSE YOUR LIFE, AND FIND IT.` · `RECEIVE YOU, RECEIVE ME.` · `A CUP OF COLD WATER ONLY.`

segments.voice: If there's water nearby, pour a glass, cold if you can, and hold it while the timer runs. Feel the weight of it and the chill against your palm. Then decide who gets the next glass you pour: someone at home, at work, at practice, someone who looks like they've been carrying a lot.
A cup of cold water. The smallest gift in the whole sending speech, and the one Jesus says won't lose its reward.
screen: `A CUP OF COLD WATER — today's word`.

segments.voice: Keep this: a cup of cold water, small enough to give before dinner. See you tomorrow.

fork.setup: a new hire on your shift is drowning on day one. you're slammed too. what's the Matthew 10 move?
options: wait until the rush is over, so you can give a real welcome.
grab them a cold water now and say you'll help after the rush.
tell the manager they need better training before next shift.
fork.reveal: the speech ends on the smallest welcome: a cup of cold water only, and it shall in no wise lose its reward. small and now beats big and later.

chat.meaning: Matthew 10:42: even a cup of cold water only, given to a little one, shall in no wise lose its reward. Small counts.

at variance.meaning: in conflict, at odds with each other

little ones.meaning: the small and humble; some readers say the disciples
